concepts.text: institutional enterprise: identifies the state as an organized, coercive operation rather than an ethical personality or ordinary firm
concepts.anchor: the naked fact that the state among us is at bottom noth­ing other than an in­sti­tu­tion­al en­ter­prise equipped with co­er­cive power

concepts.text: extensive and intensive operation: supplies comparative dimensions linking territorial scale, administrative intensity, and rationality
concepts.anchor: Or­di­nar­i­ly the ex­ten­sive mode of op­er­a­tion is at the same time the ir­ra­tional one; with in­ten­si­ty, ra­tio­nal­i­ty grows as well.

concepts.text: state interest: attributes to the state an interest in preserving and perfecting its indispensable bureaucratic machinery
concepts.anchor: Its preser­va­tion and per­fec­tion is a state in­ter­est of the very high­est rank.

concepts.text: power and rule: names the specifically political ends distinguishing state enterprise from economic enterprise
concepts.anchor: one might indeed also de­scribe the state as an un­der­tak­ing — not, of course, an eco­nom­ic one, but one di­rect­ed toward the ends of power and rule.
